research_question: Can a bounded reject-only MiniLM prefilter reduce CPU routing latency while preserving the validated sibling-contrastive BGE supported-operation profile and near-domain unsupported-operation rejection?

selection_policy.candidate_confirmation_data: v5 calibration split only after candidate freeze
forbidden_for_selection: any v15 generated corpus or result
selection_policy.primary_objective: minimize paired mean CPU latency among candidates meeting both quality floors
selection_policy.tie_breaker: higher harmonic mean of supported-operation routed accuracy and near-domain unsupported-operation rejection

candidate_family.primary_stage: multilingual MiniLM operation similarity used only for conservative fast rejection
candidate_family.escalation_stage: frozen beta=1 sibling-contrastive BGE for every non-rejected batch
candidate_family.prohibited_fast_path: MiniLM may not fast-accept or select an endpoint; non-rejected choices always escalate to BGE
candidate_family.authority_constraint: the prefilter may only suppress an already-authorized sibling-operation batch; it cannot add, select, reorder, or create execution authority

isolation_requirements: No normalized exact-query overlap with v2-v14 evidence corpora.
The v15 corpus must not exist before the complete reject-only candidate is frozen.
The generator and frozen candidate configuration must be committed before the one-shot run starts.
A runtime seed must be recorded with the generated corpus and result artifact.
The generated corpus must not be opened, previewed, summarized, or used for any configuration change before scoring completes.
After the first completed scoring run, v15 is permanently consumed and may be used only for reporting or clearly labeled diagnostics.
